tools.name: check_email
tools.description: Checks one email address the way a signup form would: invalid syntax, disposable/throwaway domain, domain that cannot receive mail (no MX), likely typo with a suggested fix (e.g. gmial.com -> gmail.com), privacy relay (Apple Hide My Email, Firefox Relay: allowed, they reach a real inbox) and role ad

tools.name: check_domains
tools.description: Checks up to 50 email domains (for example the domains of recent signups) and says which are disposable, which cannot receive mail, and which look fine. Send only domains, never full addresses.

tools.name: same_inbox
tools.description: Compares two addresses after normalising Gmail dots, +tags and googlemail.com. Use it to spot one person signing up again for a free trial with an alias (j.ane+2@gmail.com vs jane@gmail.com).

tools.name: how_to_block
tools.description: Returns setup steps and links for blocking disposable and fake signups on a given stack: next.js, supabase, clerk, better-auth, auth.js, firebase, laravel, django, or html (any form: Webflow, Framer, WordPress).

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_email, check_domains · Public sink: check_email, check_domains.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_email, check_domains · Public sink: check_email, check_domains

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
